headline: Write DESIGN.md prose that AI agents actually follow design rules
summary: LLMs read markdown with high fidelity, making prose an ideal channel for design intent. Learn how to describe intent and rules, not just values, to guide AI agents effectively.
details: To make AI agents follow design rules, DESIGN.md emphasizes describing intent and rules, not just values. While a token defines a color, good prose explains its purpose, like 'for the primary action only'.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are highly adept at reading markdown, as much of their training data is structured this way. This makes prose an effective medium for conveying complex design intent and rules to AI agents.

Test DESIGN.md prose by asking if an unfamiliar designer could apply your system correctly. Write what prevents mistakes, focusing on 'Do's and Don'ts' sections to directly address common agent errors.

Tokens define values, but the rationale behind them is crucial for establishing identity. Spend time on prose that transforms these values into your brand's unique design language, enabling agents to generalize rules beyond explicit examples.
A free 'DESIGN.md Quick-Start Cheat Sheet' is available, offering the format, an annotated example, and the core idea. This resource helps you get started quickly.
For a deeper understanding, 'DESIGN.md: The Complete Guide' covers the entire format. It includes details on token schema, CLI, accessibility, Tailwind and DTCG export, and agent integration.

headline_marked: [[0deps Movement]] proposes local dependencies for enhanced software supply chain security
headline: 0deps Movement proposes local dependencies for enhanced software supply chain security
summary: The 0deps model aims to drastically reduce software supply chain risks by incorporating all dependencies directly into project repositories, eliminating dynamic downloads and centralizing control.
details: For years, software development has relied on installing dozens, even hundreds, of external libraries, leading to thousands of transitive dependencies. This widespread practice, while accelerating development, has introduced significant software supply chain risks.

The 0deps model proposes a fundamental shift: every required dependency is incorporated directly into the project repository. This means dependencies are no longer downloaded dynamically by package managers during installation or build processes.

A core principle is that applications interact exclusively with stable internal contracts, isolating external integrations behind internal adapters. This design ensures that implementations can evolve without affecting how the rest of the application interacts with a library.

This isolation dramatically reduces the impact of technology changes and security vulnerabilities. If an external library becomes deprecated or unsupported, only its adapter needs to change, allowing applications to continue functioning without requiring extensive code modifications.

The goal of 0deps is to significantly reduce software supply chain risk by eliminating dynamic dependency installation during builds. Every line of executable code becomes part of the project itself, enabling centralized auditing, version control, and security review.

This approach results in software that is more predictable, resilient, and easier to maintain over the long term. It allows applications to continue functioning consistently for many years, centralizing responsibility for ecosystem adaptations within the project itself.
